conventions.convention: O(g) and o(g) are eventual inequalities without division: f(n) <= C g(n) for all large n, resp. f(n) <= eps g(n) for every eps > 0 and all large n, so zeros of g on the tail force zeros of f there; O_M constants may depend on the fixed description M but not on the input word, its length, or an external clock, and a two-parameter bound T_M(x,b) = O_M(G(n,b)) means a single C_M valid for every valid (x,b), b = 0 and b = 1 included.

Time is the number of executed transitions; space is the sum over tapes of the cells actually scanned, each initial head cell included, and a head's scanned cells form an initial segment; initialized but unscanned input is not counted; worst-case cost at length n is the maximum over the finitely many words of that length and is set to zero when there are none; no bound is asserted for a nonhalting run; space excluding a read-only input tape must be labelled separately.

Canonical numerals and inputs: bin(0) is the one-letter word 0, every positive numeral starts with 1 with no leading zeros, unary input for n is 1^n (the empty word at n = 0), constructibility guards t(n) >= n+1 with t nondecreasing, and exact-clock constructibility is a separate interface with a nonhalting initial state and last transition into a halting state, so no value zero is admissible.

A numeric output is canonical iff it is the single bit 0 or starts with 1; the empty output is invalid rather than the numeral zero; the output word is the maximal initial tape segment whose letters lie in {1,2} (letters 1,2 carry bits 0,1), and an accepting or rejecting last state does not change this.

Indices run over the binary words in length-lexicographic order starting with the empty word: index e denotes the word obtained by deleting the leading 1 from bin(e+1), and conversely the index of a word w is 2^{|w|} - 1 + val(w).

Configuration codes are [q,h,v] with q < m and all symbols < r, trimmed by l(v) >= h+1 and either l(v) = h+1 or a nonblank last symbol, i.e. trimmed through the larger of head position and last nonblank position; coordinates beyond l(v) are the blank symbol 0; malformed programs (in particular codes with fewer than two input letters, so s >= 2 is required) and invalid terminal output denote the nowhere-defined numeric function.

Arity-k machine input is the published prefix-free tuple word E(bin(a_1),...,bin(a_k)) = 1^k 0 c(bin(a_1))...c(bin(a_k)) with c(w) = 1^{|w|}0w, including its unary arity header, with bits 0,1 rewritten as machine letters 1,2; the empty parameter tuple is not an arity-zero machine input, so unary evaluation carries the one-entry tuple wrapper.

The symbol for partial-function equality means equality of domains and of values; composition is strict, so a divergent subcall makes the composite diverge, and minimization evaluates g(a,0), g(a,1), ... sequentially with no dovetailing past an undefined value.

Reduction orientation and totality: A <=_m B is witnessed by a total computable f with (n in A iff f(n) in B), direction from the source membership problem into the target; A <=_T B is witnessed by a total B-oracle program outputting A's characteristic bit; malformed input numerals impose no requirement, and a malformed oracle query answers zero.

PTM probabilities live on the finite space {0,1}^{p(n)} with mass 2^{-p(n)}, one fresh independent fair bit per nonhalting transition and unused suffix bits ignored after halting; a polynomial-time PTM halts on every branch within p(|x|) transitions, so every word of the space determines a halting branch.

Class thresholds are one-sided by input side and each class quantifies one fixed PTM: RP a(x) >= 1/2 on L and a(x) = 0 off L; coRP a(x) = 1 on L and a(x) <= 1/2 off L; BPP a(x) >= 2/3 on L and a(x) <= 1/3 off L; PP a(x) > 1/2 on L and a(x) <= 1/2 off L (strict majority, no bounded-error gap); ZPP expected runtime is the survival sum E T = sum_{j >= 0} q_j with q_j the fraction of length-j bit words not halted after j transitions, and probability-one halting means q_j -> 0.

The tail estimates require mutual independence (pairwise independence alone is not substituted) of Bernoulli variables on a finite probability space and cover mu = 0, N = 0, delta = 0 and delta = 1; the affine hash family is only pairwise independent, given by the count condition with uniform marginals, zero slopes included and distinct seeds allowed to give the same function.

Schwartz-Zippel is stated for a nonzero formal polynomial (not a function) of total degree d over a finite field, a nonempty sample set A with independent uniform coordinates, and the bound min(1, d/|A|); formal degree is separated from the induced zero function.

load_bearing.statement: Addition, multiplication, truncated subtraction, comparisons, bounded sums and products, bounded search, and exponentiation are primitive recursive (PR). Use pair(a,b) = 2^a(2b+1), nil = 0, cons(a,z) = pair(a,z). ... List length, coordinate (zero beyond the length), reverse, append of one entry, concatenation and bounded list predicates are PR.

For each arity k >= 0, primitive recursive functions are total maps N^k -> N given by finite derivation trees from rules [zero, successor, projections; composition; primitive recursion f(a,0) = g(a), f(a,y+1) = h(a,y,f(a,y))]; this is the least arity-indexed class closed under the rules.

A history is a list of such configuration codes. The predicate T_k(e,a,z) holds precisely when: the program is valid with at least two input letters; z is a nonempty history; its first entry is the initial configuration on the specified tuple; every entry except the last is nonhalting; each adjacent pair satisfies the one-step configuration relation; and the last entry is in state 1 or 2 with canonical numeric output.

For each fixed positive k, the predicate T_k and total output function U of the preceding definition are primitive recursive. The predicate holds exactly on histories of a terminating canonical-numeric computation. For fixed e,a, every witness has the same output U(z).

For each fixed positive arity k, the numerical partial function of program index e has normal form phi_e^{(k)}(a) = U(mu z T_k(e,a,z)). ... This class is exactly the numerical partial functions computed by Turing machines under the fixed encodings.

It is acceptable in the composition formulation used here if evaluation (e,x) -> phi_e(x) is partial computable and there is a total computable c: N^2 -> N with phi_{c(e,d)}(x) equal to phi_e(phi_d(x)) (same domain and values).

For all positive m,n there is a total computable specialization function s_m^n such that phi_{s_m^n(e,a_1,...,a_m)}^{(n)}(y_1,...,y_n) = phi_e^{(m+n)}(a_1,...,a_m,y_1,...,y_n), equality including domains.

For f,g: N -> [0,infinity), write f = O(g) if there are real C > 0 and N in N such that f(n) <= C g(n) for every n >= N ... Time is the number of executed transitions. For a finite run, space is the sum, over tapes, of the numbers of cells actually scanned, including each initial head cell.

The bound t is time constructible in this interface if a fixed deterministic multitape transducer reads that unary input completely, writes bin(t(n)) on its output tape, and halts in at most C t(n) transitions for one fixed C and all n.
For A,B subsets of N, write A <=_m B if a total computable f: N -> N satisfies for all n: (n in A iff f(n) in B). Direction is from the membership problem A to the target B.

A machine is polynomial time if it halts on every input of length n in at most C(n+1)^k transitions, for fixed positive integer C and nonnegative integer k. ... A verifier consists of a binary relation R decided in time polynomial in |x|+|w|+1, together with an explicit nonnegative integer polynomial witness guard p.
It is polynomial time if one fixed integer polynomial p bounds the number of transitions on every random branch on every input x by p(|x|).
A family (h_k: D -> R) is pairwise independent if each h_k(x) is uniform on R and, for distinct x,y in D and all u,v in R, |{k: h_k(x)=u, h_k(y)=v}|/|K| = 1/|R|^2.

Let F be a finite field, m >= 1, and f in F[x_1,...,x_m] a nonzero formal polynomial of total degree d. For a nonempty subset A of F and independent uniform a_i in A, P(f(a_1,...,a_m)=0) <= min(1, d/|A|).

concerns.concern: Step 3.1 describes each virtual tape's buffers as already holding the input cells 1,2,... and then blanks, while step 8.1 says to initialise only the centres and to materialise each level lazily from an archive, calling an unallocated zone's records 'untouched initial half-full lists'. The invariant 'ignoring holes and concatenating the zones gives the exact two stacks' is therefore asserted for zones whose record contents are deferred, and a reader must reconcile the two descriptions and check that the archive pointer sits exactly at the next untouched cell when a level is first reached (including when another virtual tape forces the allocation first).

The time count in steps 7.1 and 9.1 charges each level-i event O_M(2^i) and uses 'at most floor(b/2^i) level-i events' plus O_M(b) table/centre work and O(b log(b+2)) clock scans. This also needs the interpreter's head travel to be charged: after a level-j redistribution all lower right zones are half-full, so the least nonempty right zone is zone 0 and a level-j event can be followed immediately by a level-0 event, forcing a sweep back over the allocated prefix. The sum is still correct if each sweep is charged to one of the two adjacent events (the head is left inside the prefix of the level just operated on) and the k fixed tapes are absorbed into the O_M constant, but that charging is nowhere stated; step 6.2's O_M(2^i) covers only the redistribution scans of the prefix.

Step 4.1 gives explicit formulas for the redistribution but asserts 'Order and complementary occupancy are preserved; every lower zone ends half-full' without checking the record order across the split of the 1 + 2*sum_{j<i} h_j = 2h_i - 1 records into the lower zones and level i; step 6.2 likewise asserts that markers yield all half-capacities 'without per-record unbounded arithmetic'. I verified the formulas for i = 0,1 and reconstructed the general split, but the text leaves the order-preservation check to the reader.

Step 2.1 applies Markov with K = 2p(n) to conclude q_{2p(n)} <= ET/(2p(n)) <= 1/2, and step 2.2 groups 'the first KP(n) survival terms'; both divide by the polynomial bound, so they need p(n) > 0 (and P(n) > 0) on every input length. The item never states that the 'fixed positive integer polynomial' is positive-valued; the companion def-probabilistic-polynomial-time-machine-interface only notes that p(n) = 0 is incompatible with an all-branch bound from a nonhalting start. The intended reading (ET >= q_0 = 1 forces p(n) >= 1) should be recorded, and the empty-input (n = 0) boundary checked under it.

Step 4.1 justifies the output scan by 'The implicit next cell is blank, so this is exactly the maximal bit prefix.' If the first coordinate of the tape list outside {1,2} is a letter >= 3 that the program wrote, that cell is not blank; the rule 'find the first coordinate not in {1,2}, using the length if no such coordinate occurs, then Horner-accumulate' still computes the maximal {1,2}-segment, so the algorithm is correct, but the stated reason is not.

The marginal clause reads 'each h_k(x) is uniform on R'; a single seed gives a single value, so uniformity is a property of the seed distribution for each fixed x, i.e. |{k: h_k(x)=u}|/|K| = 1/|R| for every u in R. The count form makes the intent recoverable, but the sentence as written attributes uniformity to a value rather than to a distribution.
